description: A South Carolina jury acquitted gas station owner Rick Chow of killing 14-year-old Cyrus Carmack-Belton, who was shot in the back while fleeing over alleged stolen bottled water he had already returned.

faqs.answer: Cyrus Carmack-Belton was a 14-year-old Black honors student from Columbia, South Carolina who loved basketball and video games. He was shot and killed on May 28, 2023 by gas station owner Rick Chow.
faqs.question: Who was Cyrus Carmack-Belton?

faqs.answer: No. Surveillance video from the Shell gas station showed that Cyrus returned the four bottles of water before leaving the store. Prosecution evidence confirmed he stole nothing.
faqs.question: Did Cyrus Carmack-Belton steal the bottled water?

faqs.answer: On June 1, 2026, after approximately eight hours of deliberation, a Richland County jury acquitted Chikei Rick Chow of all charges related to the shooting death of Cyrus Carmack-Belton.
faqs.question: What was the jury's verdict in the Rick Chow trial?

faqs.answer: Yes. The family filed a civil lawsuit in 2024 that was stayed pending the outcome of the criminal trial. With the criminal case now concluded, the civil lawsuit will move forward.
faqs.question: Can the Carmack-Belton family still pursue civil action?

leadParagraph: Chikei Rick Chow shot 14-year-old Cyrus Carmack-Belton in the back at a Columbia, SC gas station over four bottles of water the boy had already returned. Surveillance footage proved Cyrus stole nothing. A jury deliberated eight hours and let his killer walk free.

methodology: Article based on court documents, surveillance footage, witness testimony, family statements, and reporting from ABC News, WLTX, WACH, Post and Courier, Legal Affairs and Trials, and Essence.
title: South Carolina Jury Acquits Store Owner Who Killed 14-Year-Old Black Teen Over Bottled Water
